subject: Recap & next steps — Novalight discovery (latency, throughput, topology)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps — Novalight discovery (latency, throughput, topology)

Alice — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick written recap and the suggested next steps so we all have the same picture.

High-level pain points you shared
- Production tail latency spikes during business hours (observed p95 ~ 480–650ms for the current model).
- Cost of scaling to handle short bursts (60–90s) of heavy traffic.
- Need for an on-prem/private option for regulated workflows plus audit logs for compliance.
- Mixed request mix: short interactive prompts (~20–80 tokens) and some long generation jobs (median ~120 tokens, max ~1k).

Goals we aligned on
- P95 latency target: <= 250ms for standard interactive requests (token lengths <= 256).
- Support peak sustained throughput of ~200 qps with graceful handling of 400 qps spikes for short windows.
- Pilot on Dedicated capacity with private-control-plane option if PoC looks good.

Technical summary & proposal (high level)
- Model family: prefer a 13B-class open model (quantized) plus a fallback 7B variant for cost-sensitive tiers.
- Runtime config: 30ms batching window, request-aware batching (separate short vs long request queues).
- KV cache: aggressive prefix caching for session-heavy traffic (expect 50–70% reuse on chat flows).
- Routing: multi-variant routing (primary high-accuracy model, fallback quantized variant) with automatic degradation to maintain latency SLOs.
- Topology: Dedicated GPU pool in us-west, autoscale policy for burst capacity, can mirror on-prem nodes for regulated workloads.

Next steps I propose
1) You share a representative sample of request traces (anonymized) and a short list of 10 representative prompts. I attached a small spreadsheet template (novalight-tech-ask-sheet.xlsx) to make this easy.
2) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with your infra and security leads. Monica and Lauren from our side will join.
3) We'll produce a short PoC plan (resource estimate, expected cost, SLO projections) within 3 business days after we get the traces.

Attachments: novalight-tech-ask-sheet.xlsx (template for request traces and payload samples)

Thanks — I captured action items on my side and will follow up with a draft mutual action plan after the deep-dive.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

Thanks Rishi — this captures it well. A couple clarifications from our side:
- Peak profile: our production forecast is ~200 qps sustained during peak windows, but we see short high-velocity bursts up to ~400 qps that typically last 60–90s (marketing campaigns + daily sync jobs).
- Token mix: as you noted, ~70% of requests are short (<=120 tokens), median ~120 tokens; long-form generation (~>512 tokens) is <5% of calls but we need to ensure it doesn't block the interactive traffic.
- Security: SOC2 is baseline; we will likely require audit-log export and integration with our SIEM. On-prem option may be needed for a subset of internal models (air-gapped).

I'm looping in ops@novalight.io — they'll provide request traces and agree a time for the deep-dive. Proposed window next Tuesday 10:00–11:00 PT (tentative).

Alice Chen
Head of Product, Novalight
alice@novalight.io

Alice — perfect, thanks for the numbers. A few technical notes ahead of the deep-dive so your infra folks have context:

SLO and capacity sketch (estimates to validate with traces)
- Target p95 latency: 250ms for interactive tier (<=256 tokens).
- Target p50/p95 for long-form: p50 ~600ms, p95 ~1.2s (we'll isolate long-form onto separate queues to avoid head-of-line blocking).
- Rough GPU sizing: for a quantized-13B variant we expect ~12–18 qps per A100-like GPU at interactive token lengths depending on the kernel path; with intelligent batching + KV cache we can raise effective throughput.
- Burst handling: autoscaling + short-term burst pool (pre-warmed instances) to sustain 400 qps for 60–90s without violating p95 for the interactive tier.

Topology proposal (sketch)
1) Dedicated inference pool in us-west for primary traffic (pinned models).
2) A small hot-pool (burst) with pre-warmed replicas to absorb short spikes.
3) Optional private deployment (on-prem) for regulated workloads with a private-control-plane sync to Redwood for observability and billing.
4) KV cache layer in front of runtime for session-heavy flows; policy to invalidate stale prefixes after 30 minutes.

Operational asks for PoC
- We need anonymized request traces (timestamps, token counts, latency per request) + a small set (10) of representative prompts.
- Security contact (who will own the SOC2/questionnaire) and list of any required compliance artifacts.

Attachments included: redwood-deploy-sketch.svg, mvp-metrics.csv (small sample perf numbers). I've also added a Drive link with a lightweight topology diagram: https://drive.redwood/example/novalight-topology-diagram

If those all look good we will produce a short PoC plan (resource estimate, timeline, success criteria) before the deep-dive. Monica will coordinate the scheduling and intake.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
